t: Not to exceed 5 percent of any appropriation made available for the current fiscal year for the National Science Foundation in this Act may be transferred between such appropriations, but no such appropriation shall be increased by more than 10 percent by any such transfers. Any transfer pursuant to this paragraph shall be treated as a reprogramming of funds under section 505 of this Act and shall not be available for obligation except in compliance with the procedures set forth in that section.  The Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate at least 30 days in advance of any planned divestment through transfer, decommissioning, termination, or deconstruction of any NSF-owned facilities or any NSF capital assets (including land, structures, and equipment) valued greater than $2,500,000.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the 30-day advance notification and the reprogramming procedures amount to consultation before a federal decision. Those notifications go only to the congressional Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. The remainder of the section governs transfers between NSF appropriations. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is given any role, so there is no participation.
fable.s: The Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate at least 30 days in advance of any planned divestment

opus.w: This section only moves money between appropriations and requires NSF to give advance notice to congressional Appropriations Committees. Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, so this notice is not participation. The section has no public comment, hearing, outside advisory body or consultation with non-federal parties.
opus.s: The Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate at least 30 days in advance of any planned divestment
opus.b: **Tempting-but-wrong reading:** The 30-day advance notice before NSF divests a facility, along with the reprogramming procedures, can look like a formal procedural step before a federal decision. But the only body involved is the House and Senate Appropriations Committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the NSF Director to notify the Congressional Committees on Appropriations before divesting assets. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government. Notification to an internal government body does not constitute participation with people outside the government.
qwen_chat.s: The Director of the National Science Foundation (NSF) shall notify the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate at least 30 days in advance of any planned divestment through transfer, decommissioning, termination, or deconstruction of any NSF-owned facilities or any NSF capital assets (including land, structures, and equipment) valued greater than $2,500,000.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that notifying the Committees on Appropriations constitutes "participation" because it involves an external body being informed before a decision is finalized. However, the definition explicitly states that "Congress, its committees and members... are all INSIDE the federal government." Therefore, notification to Congress is intra-governmental communication, not participation with outside parties.
